extraction.name: DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset for visual question answering on document images, consisting of 50,000 questions defined on 12,767 document images from UCSF Industry Documents Library, with train/validation/test splits and question type annotations.
extraction.creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from UCSF Industry Documents Library. The authors downloaded documents from different collections, hand picked pages for use in the dataset, prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures, and minimized binarized images due to quality concerns. Questions and answers were collected from these selected document images using remote workers through a web-based annotation tool in a three-stage process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: If a worker found a question inapt owing to language issues or ambiguity, the question could be flagged and such questions were not included in the dataset. If none of the answers from stage 1 matched any answers from stage 2, the item was sent for third-stage review.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images from UCSF Industry Documents Library, drawn from 6,071 industry documents spanning multiple decades and five industries: tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, and chemical.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Documents used span from 1900 to 2018; the paper does not specify the exact collection dates for downloading/annotation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Pages were hand picked from downloaded documents; binarized images were minimized; pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized over pages with only running text.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were required to be answerable using text present in the image and answers had to be entered verbatim from the document. Questions flagged for language issues or ambiguity were excluded. For reading-comprehension baselines, OCR tokens were serialized top-left to bottom-right and answer spans were approximated by first string match.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was done in three stages using remote workers and a web-based annotation tool. Stage 1: workers viewed a document image and defined up to 10 question-answer pairs, optionally providing more than one ground-truth answer per question. Stage 2: another worker saw the image and questions (without answers), entered answers, assigned one or more question types, and could flag invalid or ambiguous questions. Stage 3: authors reviewed cases where stage 1 and stage 2 answers did not exactly match, editing or accepting question-answer pairs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions were verified by comparing answers from stage 1 and stage 2; if no exact match was found, the item was reviewed by the authors in stage 3. Multiple ground-truth answers were allowed when warranted. Questions could be flagged for ambiguity or language issues and excluded.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 10 question-answer pairs per document image in stage 1; one or more answers could be provided per question.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Remote workers; the paper does not specify further demographics.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Commercial OCR solution was used to generate OCR tokens for analysis and experiments.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to advance document image understanding and purpose-driven DAR research, enabling systems to answer ad-hoc information requests from document images.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is biased toward documents from UCSF Industry Documents Library, especially from the 1960-2000 period, and includes documents from five industries. The authors also prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures and minimized binarized images, which may bias the dataset toward clearer, information-dense pages.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that many documents in the source library are binarized and image quality can be poor; such images were minimized. The dataset is limited to document images from the UCSF Industry Documents Library and may not generalize to other document domains. Questions requiring understanding of structure, figures, handwriting, or OCR quality remain challenging for models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Visual question answering on document images; training, validation, and testing of VQA and reading-comprehension-style models; baseline evaluation and benchmarking.
